what_happened: The research report classified the gate 24 dead-command-recommendation findings (/ide in the memory extension's memory-setup.md and memory-troubleshooting.md) as out of scope, but reading test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's baseline block (lines 196-203) shows its fixture-clean assertion requires baseline_rc -eq 0 from a full --max-cost moderate verify-deploy run, not merely zero gate20 findings. The live run confirms verify-deploy FAILs 2 of 40 checks on that fixture: gate20 (the eager overage this task owns) plus gate24 (the two /ide lines). Moving eager_load.baseline_bytes therefore clears only one of the two currently-failing suite cases; the baseline-fixture-clean case stays red until the separately-owned built-in-command lint-exemption record lands, and that record explicitly rejects rewording the two memory docs as the fix while another record declares that directory in its own file_scope. Consequence for the plan: the dispatch's instruction to REMOVE the known-failures.txt row cannot be satisfied; the row must be rewritten to re-attribute the residual to the cross-owned gate24 dependency instead, or run-all.sh --fail-on-new would start reporting this suite as a NEW failure.

Sourcing scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh and calling suite_selection_select directly over the two tracked paths returned the covering suites in one call (config -> test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh; known-failures.txt -> four run-all/gate8 consumer suites), so both phases' tier declarations and the Phase 2 --only list are selector-verified rather than guessed. Checking verify-deploy.sh's own BUDGET_CONFIG line (1777) in the same pass also removed a planned deployed-tree sync step outright: gate 20 reads the source store, never .claude/, so the plan needs no deploy action at all -- which the plan validator independently confirmed by warning against the .claude/** paths the first draft had declared.
